Reanalyses of some studies have led to different interpretations of the results, with some workers concluding that the risk of cancer from formaldehyde is greater than originally thought.4 Analysis of mortality data5 for a cohort of 25619 workers exposed to formaldehyde in the USA found some evidence of an association with nasopharyngeal cancer and possibly cancers at other upper respiratory-tract sites. Based on the results of this large cohort study and supported by evidence from other epidemiological and animal studies, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) concluded,6 in 2004, that occupational exposure to formaldehyde does cause nasopha- ryngeal cancer. Furthermore, they found strong, but not suffi- cient, evidence to establish a causal link with leukaemia and lim- ited evidence to suggest it causes sinonasal cancer. IARC has concluded that formaldehyde is a definite human carcinogen.6 1. Gérin M, et al.
